findings.reason: naming the reader it will extend changes the plan from "add a git-reading script" to "call the existing revision reader", a decision the author must make explicitly.
findings.text: the plan cites one existing mechanism (the routing token estimator at reckon/crew/routing.py:3158) but proposes two new ones — a base-revision source reader in `scripts/check_pure_move.py` (§2) and a map-node census of "every name some other file imports from `reckon.crew.dispatch`, every test that patches a `dispatch` attribute, and every test that reads the file's text by path" (§3) — without citing `reckon/velocity.py:424 read_sources`, `reckon/interface_counts.py:553 read_trees`, or `reckon/served_code.py`'s importer index, so the author cannot see that the reading half of the move check already exists to be extended

findings.reason: naming the owning reader turns a new git-parsing script and a hand-rolled census into an extension of `read_trees` / `_import_targets`, and prevents a second revision reader drifting from the first.
findings.text: `scripts/check_pure_move.py` re-implements machinery the repository already owns: reading a module's sources at an arbitrary revision out of git is `reckon/velocity.py:424 read_sources(repo, revision, *, prefix="")`; reading parsed trees at a revision is `reckon/interface_counts.py:553 read_trees(reckon, revision)` (with `definitions(tree)` at reckon/interface_counts.py:74); and mapping names to the module that owns them, and to the names a module imports, is `reckon/served_code.py:213 _import_targets` with `reckon/served_code.py:405 _used_definitions` (with `_definition_nodes` at reckon/served_code.py:363 and the revision-aware `_git` reader at reckon/served_code.py:90). The §3 map census ("every name some other file imports from `reckon.crew.dispatch`", "every test that patches a `dispatch` attribute", "every test that reads the file's text by path") is that importer index walked a second time. tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py:20-32 already shows the exact base-vs-head read the move check needs — layering working-tree bytes over `interface_counts.read_trees(ROOT, revision)`. Separately, the context-fit check itself already measures per-file token estimates over a node's write paths (`_context_file_inputs`, reckon/crew/routing.py:3262); §2's guard could call it rather than walk the tree itself, though a whole-tree walk is arguably a different question

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the split decomposes one oversize module into cohesive siblings, each holding one concern behind its own module interface; the original survives only as the import surface the split-surface decision justifies, so complexity is concentrated rather than spread across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `scripts/check_pure_move.py` reads a module at a base revision by shelling `git show` and `ast.parse`-ing it, and the §3 map census scans every file for the names it imports and the tests that read it by path; both duplicate readers the repository already owns — `read_sources` at reckon/velocity.py:424, `read_trees` at reckon/interface_counts.py:553, and the importer index at reckon/served_code.py:213 (`_import_targets`) and reckon/served_code.py:405 (`_used_definitions`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1528, cli_options 323, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. A pure move relocates each definition rather than adding one (§8 states no public name is added beyond the new module paths, and re-export lines are imports the counter does not count), §4 keeps every subcommand registered under the same name (no cli_options delta), and §7 keeps every tool registered on the same server under the same name (no mcp_views delta), so no section adds to any of the four families.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan reuses the context-fit token estimator (`_tokens_for_bytes`, reckon/crew/routing.py:3158) and its launch-context floor, but proposes `scripts/check_pure_move.py` reading a module at a base revision from git and a map-node census scanning every file for importers and text-by-path readers, without citing the revision-source reader or the module/importer index that already exist in this repository.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only thin layer is the original module left as a re-export/import surface, and the plan states why callers cannot be repointed instead (peer worktrees import the original paths today); that is the justification the item asks for, recorded in decision `split-surface`.
